To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the anterior cingulate is more active when response preparation and interference do not share modality than when they do share modality, that is, when the interference is not response-level.
the anterior cingulate is activated in response to cognitive conflict.

(a) anterior cingulate activation is modulated by task difficulty in a way that is not explained by the level of response-level conflict and (b) activation in this region in the Stroop task is not specific to response-level conflict.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the anterior cingulate in attention and cognitive control, particularly in response competition.
the role of the anterior cingulate in cognitive control.
the role of anterior cignulate cortex (ACC).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ACC activity in the Stroop task is a function of the amount of cognitive conflict.
ACC activity is associated with response competition and not with response selection or response preparation per se.
ACC is not involved in response-level conflict, and is involved in conflict at the level of generalized modality-independent attentional selection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ACC is involved in the detection of conflict, but only when it is response-level in nature, and only when the conflict is between competing responses.
the anterior cingulate plays a role in the selection of response alternatives, but only when there is conflict among them.

the ACC is involved in a conflict monitoring process that occurs during the response selection stage of cognitive control, and that this conflict monitoring process is sensitive to the degree of conflict.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the role of the anterior cingulate is to resolve conflicts that are not modality specific, such as response conflict.
the ACC is involved in the resolution of conflict between competing responses.
the anterior cingulate may be more sensitive to the conflict between the response to be made and the response that is being prepared.
